document.title: Rabbani Emissary States Rabbani Will Not Surrender Power to Interim Council Until Taliban Join
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] Embassy officials meet Rabbani's Economic Advisor Ashraf Shah, who summarizes events including Taliban capture of Charasiab, Maydan Shahr, Chowk-i-Wardak and the Ghazni-Kabul road. He says the government would probably not give up power to an Interim Council until the Taliban agreed to join.

events.description: Ashraf Shah meets US Ambassador and Pol/Econ chief in Dushanbe seeking US advice on transfer of power.
Radio Khorasan reports Taliban took Paktika without a fight.
Taliban defeat Hekmatyar at Charasiab; Masud's forces briefly enter then vacate; Taliban take Maydan Shahr, Chowk-i Wardak.
Date Rabbani was supposed to transfer power to Mestiri's interim council.
U.S. Embassy Dushanbe cable requests Department guidance on U.S. policy toward Mestiri's planned interim council and the transfer of power, to share with Shah, the Rabbani emissary.
Ashraf Shah, Rabbani's emissary, met US Ambassador and Pol/Econ chief seeking US advice on the Taliban and the interim council; he argued Rabbani should not hand over power until the Taliban join.
Shah arrived in Dushanbe from Moscow, en route back to Kabul via Tashkent and New Delhi.
Taliban took control of Paktika province without a fight, as Jamiat and Harikat forces handed it over.

Taliban defeated Hekmatyar's forces at Charasiab; Masud's forces entered a day before the Taliban and later vacated at Taliban request; Taliban also took Maydan Shahr, Chowk-i Wardak and the Ghazni-Kabul road, controlling all Wardak.
Hekmatyar reportedly fled to Laghman, leaving Sarobi.
Date Rabbani was supposed to turn over power to Mestiri's interim council.

key_claims: Shah portrayed the Taliban as predominantly Durrani Pashtun, rural and socially conservative, controlling six provinces with some popular support from disarming factions and restoring security.
Shah argued Rabbani should not transfer power to the UN-backed interim council unless the Taliban join it.
Shah claimed Hekmatyar was a spent force, confined to Laghman after losing Charasiab.
Shah saw only three significant forces: Taliban, Dostum's Jombesh, and the government of Rabbani, Masud and Ismail Khan.
The US urged Rabbani to transfer power to Mestiri's interim council under UN auspices, warning refusal could give the Taliban an excuse to attack Kabul.
Radio Khorasan reported Jamiat and Nabi's forces effectively handed Paktika to the Taliban.
